name: Release evidence gate
summary: A build becomes a release candidate only when version-bound evidence satisfies every declared platform, performance, persistence, accessibility, installation, update, offline, and recovery stop condition.
player_action: The player installs, configures, plays, suspends, updates, resumes, migrates, and recovers the candidate on a supported target.
system_response: The release process binds test evidence to the exact artifact and blocks unsupported targets or unresolved failures instead of averaging them into an overall pass.
failure_modes: Evidence belongs to a different build or configuration.
A platform-wide average hides one unsupported target.
Known save, crash, or accessibility failures ship without a declared boundary.
A passing checklist cannot regenerate its observations.
accessibility: Accessibility failures are release failures within the declared support boundary, not optional polish.
The gate and evidence viewer must themselves support accessible review workflows.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Build one signed candidate, deliberately fail one target in each production area, and require the gate to name the exact artifact, configuration, evidence, owner, and stop condition before any release decision.
measure: false pass and false block rate
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: The gate blocks every injected failure, accepts the corrected artifact, and can regenerate all decisive observations from bound evidence.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: The decision is correct but evidence collection makes frequent releases impractical.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Any stale, averaged, missing, or self-declared evidence permits a failing candidate or grants deployment authority by itself.

notes: Provisional until it blocks injected failures in a real build pipeline; the record defines applicability and stop conditions, not deployment authority.
